title: Left Rotate by One
directAnswer: Stash `nums[0]`, shift `nums[i] = nums[i+1]` for all i, then put the stashed value in the last slot. O(n) time, O(1) space.

rules: Drop saved value at the end.
remember.takeaway: Always snapshot the value an in-place shift will clobber.
remember.formula: t=a[0]; shift left; a[n-1]=t   (k: three reversals)

problemStatement: Given an integer array `nums`, rotate it left by one position: the first element moves to the end.
understanding: Save the first element, shift everything one slot left, then drop the saved value at the end.

examples.explanation: First element wraps to the back.

approaches.name: Shift with saved head
approaches.whenToMention: This is the standard, expected solution — lead with it.
approaches.explanation:
Rotating left by one slides every element down one index and wraps the head to the tail. Save the first element, shift, then drop it at the end.

**Why save the head first.** The shift `nums[i] = nums[i+1]` overwrites `nums[0]` on the very first step, so you must capture the original head *before* the loop, then place it in the last slot afterward. Skipping the save loses it.

**Why the loop stops at n−2.** The last write is `nums[n-2] = nums[n-1]`; going to `nums[n-1] = nums[n]` reads off the end. After the loop, `nums[n-1]` is set to the saved head.

**Rotating by k.** A left rotation by k is best done with the **three-reversal trick**: reverse the first k, reverse the rest, reverse the whole — O(n) time, O(1) space, no big temp array. Mentioning that generalisation is the standout move.
hints: Which element gets overwritten first, and how do you preserve it?
Save nums[0], shift everything left by one, then place it at the end.
Watch the upper bound so you don't read nums[n].
approaches.complexityReasoning: one shift per element with a single saved value — linear time, constant space.
